title: Calibrated Evidence Playbook — 90d prep
content:
Purpose / quick note:
- This is my personal prep doc for the next 1:1s and the informal calibration with L3 managers (Mar–Apr).
- Goal: synthesize clear examples + metrics that map to expectations for Senior People Partner (or equivalent) — focus on impact, scope, and coaching evidence.

Top priorities (right now):
1) Baseline: reduce new hire time-to-productivity (TTP) for Platform Eng hires by 2 weeks across Q1 onboarding cohort (target: -15%).
2) Launch pilot manager enablement program (MGR-Enable) -> 10 managers in cohort, collect 8 qualitative manager stories and 3 measurable manager-satisfaction delta scores.
3) Build out promotion rubric artifacts and run 1 calibration workshop with Eng+Product managers by end of April.

90-day objectives (how I will measure progress):
- Onboarding TTP: baseline = 8.6 weeks (cohort Nov–Dec), target = 7.3 weeks by end of Q2. Data source: onboarding survey + hiring manager check-ins (see JIRA-3421).
- Manager Enablement: complete cohort plan + pilot run (Mar 15–Apr 15); success = 60%+ managers report "more effective 1:1s" in post-pilot survey.
- Promotion rubric: 1 published draft + 1 cross-functional calibration session with 12 managers.

Evidence bank (concise bullets I can cite):
- Example A (scope & outcome): Feb 02 — Led cross-functional triage for Platform Eng ramp blockers: coordinated infra team, onboarding buddy rotations, and revised first-week checklist -> two hires had first PRs merged by day 9 (previous median: day 18).
  - Quote to use: "Amelie reorganized the onboarding flow so we could unblock new hires faster — immediate win." — Damian (Eng manager).
  - Artifact: github.com/redwood-inference/people-ops/PR-421 (first-week-checklist).

- Example B (coaching & multiplicative impact): Jan 21–Mar 01 — 1:1 coaching series with three mid-level managers to improve retro cadence + OKR alignment. All three reported clearer priorities and delivered on a cross-team sprint that reduced incident backlog by 22% (measured in incident ticket counts).

- Example C (systems change): Feb 15 — drafted and ran a 75-min workshop on "Effective 1:1s" for 18 managers; follow-up survey (n=12) showed +0.5 pts avg improvement in manager confidence (5-pt scale).

Behavioral/leadership evidence (mapping to rubric):
- Problem solving: reorganized onboarding; measurable TTP delta for Platform Eng hires.
- Influence: got buy-in from Eng leads + SRE to change buddy rotation policy in 2 weeks.
- Coaching: documented coaching notes for 6 managers; two promoted to lead roles in orgs where I coached them (signal of multiplicative impact).

Draft script for manager 1:1 (10–15 min):
- Opening (30s): "Thanks for making time — I want to share progress on three things and ask for your input on priority and a calibration ask."
- Quick wins (2 min): 1–2 bullets from Evidence bank; call out metric.
- Ask (2 min): "I'm preparing to request a promotion/level calibration later this quarter — I'd appreciate your candid feedback on whether the examples I listed show sufficient scope and impact, and whether you would endorse."
- Specific ask phrasing: "Would you be willing to provide a short note (1–2 sentences) about [example A] and the observed outcomes? It will help me in calibration."
- Close (30s): agree next step + timeline for when I'll share the consolidated evidence packet (target: Apr 1).

Concrete asks I will make (and why):
- Request manager endorsement note (1–2 sentences) for 2–3 signature examples. Rationale: increases signal during calibration.
- Ask for a calibration slot or to be included in the promotion runbook review. Rationale: ensure artifacts are judged with consistent rubric.
- Ask for feedback on the promotion rubric draft. Rationale: iterate quickly and make artifacts stronger and defensible.

Potential pushback & quick counters:
- "We don't have headcount for a new level": emphasize that ask is about recognition, not immediate hiring; show how my work reduced ramp time -> net capacity gain.
- "Examples are small scale": show multiplicative outcomes (e.g., reduced incident backlog, managers promoted).

Open questions / blockers I need to resolve before calibration:
- Need clearer metric ownership for onboarding TTP (who owns the dashboard?). Action: ping analytics (Diego) to add TTP to People Ops dashboard (ticket open).
- Can I get an aggregated manager-feedback metric for workshops (consistent before/after)? Action: standardize post-workshop survey template.

Follow-ups (short todo list):
- [ ] Consolidate 6 strongest examples into one slide + 1-paragraph context each (due: Mar 20).
- [ ] Send manager note template and ask for endorsements (target send: Mar 22).
- [ ] Sync with Diego on data sources for onboarding TTP (by Mar 12) — DONE (left comment on JIRA-3421).
- [ ] Finalize promotion rubric draft and share with product HR partner (Lena) for initial review (due: Mar 28).

Notes to self (quick mental shorthand):
- Keep stories concrete: role, scope, decision, outcome (numbers if possible).
- Use manager quotes — they speak louder than my interpretation.
- Anticipate calibration questions about scope: proactively show number of managers influenced, orgs impacted, and time horizon.

Rough evidence table (short):
- Onboarding flow rewrite -> metric: median time to first PR (day) down from 18 -> 9 for two hires (Feb cohort).
- Manager enablement pilot -> metric: post-pilot manager confidence +0.5 (n=12).
- Incident backlog sprint -> metric: incident ticket count down 22% after coaching initiative.

Final paragraph (prep posture):
- This doc is a living scratchpad. I will trim into a 1-page packet for manager reviews and a 2-slide executive summary for calibration. Keep notes informal here, but commit to 'clean' artifacts by Mar 20.

------

- 2026-03-08: updated manager enablement pilot dates + added survey baseline.
